
🛡️  Bedrock protection — account audit
   Account: 111111111111    Region: us-east-1
   Audit only — this command makes no changes.

── Root user — unconstrainable by design ──

  ❌ [CRITICAL] Root account MFA
     Root user has NO MFA device. Root cannot be constrained by SCPs or permission boundaries, so a compromised root is unbounded.
     → Attach a FIDO2 security key to root — phishing resistant, unlike TOTP. In Amazon-internal Isengard accounts root is managed for you and this may not be actionable; confirm before escalating.

  ✅ [CRITICAL] Root access keys
     No root access keys.

── IAM users and access keys ──

  ❓ [HIGH] Long-lived access keys
     Credential report unavailable (AccessDenied).
     → Grant iam:GenerateCredentialReport and iam:GetCredentialReport, then re-run.

  ❓ [HIGH] Console users without MFA
     Credential report unavailable (AccessDenied).
     → Grant iam:GenerateCredentialReport and iam:GetCredentialReport, then re-run.

  ❌ [HIGH] AdministratorAccess on IAM users
     AdministratorAccess is attached directly to: alice. Any access key belonging to these users is an unbounded credential.
     → Move admin access behind an assumable role gated on MFA, so no static key carries it.

  ❓ [MEDIUM] Unused credentials
     Credential report unavailable (AccessDenied).
     → Grant iam:GenerateCredentialReport and iam:GetCredentialReport, then re-run.

── Account-wide policy ──

  ❌ [MEDIUM] Account password policy
     No password policy is set, so only AWS defaults apply (minimum length 8, no complexity or reuse rules).
     → Set MinimumPasswordLength >= 14 with complexity and reuse prevention — or remove console passwords entirely in favour of Identity Center.

── Spend ceilings — both billing surfaces ──

  ❌ [HIGH] Budget covering Bedrock services
     No budgets exist in this account, so runaway Bedrock spend has no ceiling and raises no alert.
     → Create a monthly budget filtered on Service contains "Bedrock", alerting at 50/80/100% to SNS.

  ❌ [HIGH] Budget covering Marketplace (Bedrock Edition) models
     No COST budget filters on AWS Marketplace. Third-party models invoked through Bedrock — Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere — bill as Marketplace subscription line items named "(Amazon Bedrock Edition)", NOT under Amazon Bedrock. A Bedrock-only budget misses them entirely, which is the most expensive blind spot here because Opus-class models are both the priciest and the likeliest target.
     → Add a second COST budget filtered on Service = AWS Marketplace, or define a Cost Category grouping both surfaces and budget on that.

  ❓ [HIGH] Bedrock budgets actually notify someone
     No COST budget covers Bedrock or Marketplace, so there is no budget whose alerting could be checked (see bedrock-budget and marketplace-budget above).

── Detection speed — how fast you find out ──

  ❓ [HIGH] Cost Explorer enabled
     Could not confirm Cost Explorer access (AccessDeniedException).

  ❓ [MEDIUM] Cost anomaly monitor covering Bedrock, with an alert subscription
     Could not list anomaly monitors (AccessDeniedException).

  ❌ [MEDIUM] CloudWatch alarm on Bedrock invocation volume
     No alarms on AWS/Bedrock metrics in us-east-1. Cost data lags 12–24h, so budgets and anomaly detection cannot catch a stolen key inside the first day. Token-count metrics are near real-time and are the only fast signal available.
     → Alarm on AWS/Bedrock Invocations and InputTokenCount with a threshold above normal peak; it fires in minutes rather than hours.

  ❌ [MEDIUM] GuardDuty AI Protection enabled (CostHarvesting detection)
     GuardDuty is not enabled in us-east-1 at all, so no detector exists to carry AI Protection. Note that scp-detection-tamper (scan-org) asserts an SCP protects GuardDuty from teardown — that guardrail is moot where GuardDuty was never turned on.
     → Enable GuardDuty in this region, then enable the AI_PROTECTION feature on the detector. Prefer enabling it org-wide from the delegated administrator so new accounts inherit it.

── Standing commitments ──

  ✅ [INFO] Provisioned Throughput commitments
     No Provisioned Throughput commitments in us-east-1. NOTE: region-scoped — a commitment in another region will not appear here.

── Forensics — can you answer "who?" ──

  ❌ [MEDIUM] Bedrock model invocation logging
     Off in us-east-1. CloudTrail records that InvokeModel was called but not the model, prompt or token counts, so during an incident you can see spend rose without being able to attribute it to a caller or workload.
     → Enable model invocation logging to CloudWatch Logs or S3. Prompts and completions are captured, so treat the destination as sensitive and scope its access accordingly.

  Findings by severity: CRITICAL 1, HIGH 3, MEDIUM 4, LOW 0
